chunks: From him, from al-Hajjāl, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Abū ʿUmārah ibn al-Ṭayyār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): 'My wealth has been lost, what is in my hand has scattered, and my dependents are many.' He said: 'When you arrive, open the door of your shop, spread out your mat, place your scales, and expose yourself to the sustenance of your Lord.'

So when he arrived, he opened his door, spread his mat, and placed his scales. Those around him from his neighbors were amazed that he had neither little nor much goods in his house, nor did he have anything.

He said: Then a man came to him and said, 'Buy me a garment.' So he bought one for him, took its price, and the price came to him. Then another man came and said, 'Buy me a garment.' So he procured the rest of the market's goods, then bought a garment for him, took its price, and it remained in his hand.
And that is what merchants do; some of them take from others.

Then a man came to him and said, 'O Abū ʿUmārah, I have two weights of linen. Will you buy them for something, and I will defer payment to you for a year?' He said, 'Yes, carry it and bring it to me.'
He said: So he carried it to him and bought it from him with a one-year deferment. The man stood up and left.
Then someone from his market people came to him and said to him, 'O Abū ʿUmārah, what is this weight?' He said to him, 'This is a weight I bought.'

He said, 'Will you sell me half of it, and I will expedite its price for you?' He said, 'Yes.' So he bought it from him, gave him half of the goods, took half the price, and the remainder remained in his hand until a year.
So he began to buy with its price the garment and the two garments, buying and selling until he became wealthy, his face was honored, and he became well-known.

key_terms.بِسَاط: Mat spread on the floor for displaying goods
key_terms.عِدْل: A weight or measure (specifically of linen here)

ai.seo_question: How did Abū ʿUmārah recover his wealth after losing everything according to the hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia scholarly endorsement of active commerce and strategic liquidity management, emphasizing that one must actively seek sustenance (*rizq*) rather than passively wait. The narrative highlights the practical application of trade ethics, where the Imam guides Abū ʿUmārah to utilize credit and resale mechanisms to generate capital from minimal assets, a method that led to his prosperity and social standing.
